transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-21
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marcus Lee (Redwood SE), Jordan Kim (Redwood CSM), Sarah Chopra (Veridian Procurement), Priya Raman (Veridian Legal), Tom Alvarez (Veridian CISO), Ben Whitmore (Veridian Cloud)

Summary:
Quick procurement onboarding and legal review: high-level on MSA/DPA redlines, SLA expectations for Dedicated vs Hosted, confirmation of SOC2 / ISO docs, KMS/Encryption and VPC requirements, pricing approval path and PO timing. Agreed to run a short benchmark and circulate redlines.

Topics:
- MSA & DPA redlines and liability caps
- SLA requirements and uptime/latency targets for dedicated capacity
- Data residency, SSO/SAML, KMS integration, audit logs
- Pricing approval and procurement timeline / PO
- Pilot scope and technical benchmark

Transcript:
[00:00] Lena Park: hey everyone thanks for joining, i'll do a quick roll call. um Marcus joining from infra, Jordan's on the line for onboarding.
[00:06] Sarah Chopra: hi yes sarah here, priya and tom and ben are with me.
[00:10] Marcus Lee: hey all, good to meet you.
[00:12] Priya Raman: hi, thanks for arranging.
[00:15] Lena Park: great, high level today is procurement and legal, make sure the redlines are understood, SLA asks, and then next steps for onboarding.
[00:22] Tom Alvarez: quick context, Veridian is moving inference workloads for our customer-facing product to a vendor-managed solution. security/topline needs: SOC2 type II, kms integration, vpc peering, and tight data retention. our procurement window is september; we need pricing signed off and PO by mid-september.
[00:40] Lena Park: understood — our typical flow is we share the redlined DPA and MSA, we can accept a limited set of commercial edits, and we also provide SOC2/ISO and security pack, also dedicated offering for higher SLOs.
[00:52] Priya Raman: on indemnity and liability cap, our legal team prefers 5M cap; can you confirm Redwood's standard? i saw 1M in the draft.
[01:05] Marcus Lee: (background) mmh — just to add on the technical side, dedicated capacity also gives you isolation and predictable throughput. for liability stuff, i'm not the right person but we can bring legal.
[01:14] Lena Park: yea, our standard is 1M but we can escalate for enterprise deals. we have a process — typically for committed reserved capacity we can discuss increasing cap; it's escalated through finance and legal.
[01:27] Priya Raman: ok please put that in writing. also, data processing terms — we need explicit subprocessor list and an option for on-prem or VPC private deployment if required later.
[01:38] Lena Park: subprocessor list is in the security pack, we'll share the full list, and we do offer Redwood Private which can be VPC or on-prem for regulated workloads. note there's a separate licensing and ops discussion for on-prem.
[01:51] Sarah Chopra: timeline — to get a PO by mid-september we need pricing approved by next week. what's the cadence for pricing approvals?
[01:59] Jordan Kim: we can provide a dedicated pricing sheet and a recommended commit. there's sometimes a procurement approval path — we usually need an internal quote sign-off and then legal sign-off.
[02:10] Ben Whitmore: technical Q — for VPC peering, what IP ranges do you need? and what's the recommended KMS integration flow? we want to run keys in our KMS.
[02:20] Marcus Lee: we support customer-managed KMS keys via our integration with common providers; we also support bring-your-own-key (BYOK) with HSM in private deployments. for hosted we can integrate via cross-account key policies, but for full BYOK you likely want Redwood Private.
[02:35] Ben Whitmore: noted. and latency SLOs for dedicated — we target 99th pct under 300ms for typical gen requests? is that right?
[02:44] Marcus Lee: it depends on model and sequence length, but for our Dedicated pools we have configurations that hit ~120-250ms 99th for short prompts on optimized models. we'll include benchmark numbers.
[02:56] Tom Alvarez: encryption at rest and in transit — are audit logs available for every request? we need 13 months of auditability.
[03:05] Lena Park: yes we keep request-level audit logs (configurable retention) and can export to customer S3 or SIEM. retention tiers can be part of the add-on.
[03:14] Sarah Chopra: payment terms — net 30 is standard for us, any issues?
[03:19] Lena Park: net 30 is fine for enterprise deals; for initial pilot we sometimes require upfront commit for Dedicated.
[03:26] Priya Raman: on data residency — some customers will require EU-only processing. can you guarantee region pinning?
[03:33] Marcus Lee: we can route workloads by region and have region pinning on Dedicated and Private. hosted API has regional routing but not strict pinning for multi-tenant unless requested as a region-only tenancy.
[03:46] Priya Raman: ok we'll flag that if needed.
[03:49] Sarah Chopra: question on DPA termination — our security policy requires secure deletion within 30 days post-termination, is that supported?
[03:58] Lena Park: yes, secure delete is supported and we can document the deletion process. our retention and deletion procedures will be in the DPA security exhibit.
[04:08] Ben Whitmore: any penalties or SLA credits for missed latency or uptime?
[04:12] Marcus Lee: we have SLA credits for uptime in Dedicated packages; latency SLOs are contractual for certain models/paths and we can include credits for repeated misses. it's in the SLA exhibit.
[04:25] Tom Alvarez: for procurement, we'll need a contact to send the redline and a copy of SOC2/ISO docs. also we may request a stronger security addendum around incident notification timelines.
[04:37] Lena Park: i'll be your primary for contracts, lena at redwood dot ai, and i'll attach SOC2 and ISO certificates. Jordan will handle onboarding schedule.
[04:46] Sarah Chopra: great. pricing question — what's the delta between hosted API and dedicated pricing? our finance wants ballpark numbers now.
[04:53] Lena Park: hosted is per-token; dedicated is a monthly reserved pool with lower per-token and guaranteed throughput. i'll share a pricing sheet but ballpark — dedicated is typically 35-50% lower unit cost depending on commit and model family.
[05:07] Sarah Chopra: that helps. we also have procurement requirements around vendor cybersecurity ratings — do you have an external attestation?
[05:14] Lena Park: yes we can share audits and third-party attestation, and we also support SSO via SAML/Okta and RBAC.
[05:22] Priya Raman: are there any unusual clauses in the MSA we should know about? data sharing, subprocessing, or right to modify service?
[05:30] Lena Park: standard clauses: change to service is covered by change management, subprocessing list is disclosed, we attempt to give notice for changes that materially impact service. we can call out any requested cosmetic edits.
[05:42] Ben Whitmore: for the technical benchmark — what are you expecting from us? traffic shape and dataset?
[05:47] Marcus Lee: yes, sample prompt sets, sequence length distribution, expected qps, concurrency. we'll run tests against a pinned model variant (quantized or fp16) and share latency and cost metrics.
[05:59] Sarah Chopra: ok timeline recap — we need pricing by 2026-08-28, redlines by 2026-08-25, benchmark scheduled the week of 2026-08-31, PO mid-september. does that align?
[06:11] Lena Park: yep that aligns. i'll get the redlined MSA/DPA over by tuesday, and Marcus will propose benchmark times.
[06:20] Priya Raman: one more — can you confirm the process for breach notification? we need 72-hour notification for incidents affecting our data.
[06:30] Lena Park: we typically commit to 72-hour initial notification and detailed follow-up as per the security exhibit. we'll include that language in the DPA.
[06:38] Tom Alvarez: fine. procurement might want premier support during onboarding window — what's the cost for premium SLA?
[06:46] Jordan Kim: premium SLA / 24x7 support and faster on-call response is an add-on. i'll include pricing options in the sheet.
[06:54] Sarah Chopra: any blockers from Redwood side for PO terms? we have standard legal redlines but nothing unusual yet.
[06:59] Lena Park: no blockers; we just need to route the redlines to our legal and finance.
[07:05] Lena Park: alright let's do a quick recap and next steps.
[07:08] Marcus Lee: recap — share benchmark plan and configs, share security pack and subprocessor list, provide pricing sheet and premium SLA options.
[07:16] Sarah Chopra: and procurement will review the redlines and attempt to consolidate comments by 2026-08-26.
[07:22] Lena Park: perfect. thanks everyone — i'll send the calendar invite for the kickoff and attach the docs.
[07:27] Priya Raman: thank you.
[07:30] (call ends)

Notes about transcription: some names and product terms may be mis-transcribed (e.g., "Redwood Dedicate" instead of "Redwood Dedicated"), timestamps approximate.

End of meeting transcript.

Recap / Next Steps (plain):
- Lena to send redlined MSA & DPA to Priya by 2026-08-25.
- Marcus to prepare benchmark runbook and propose windows the week of 2026-08-31.
- Ben to provide VPC peering details and KMS policies by 2026-08-28.
- Jordan to share premium SLA / support pricing.
- Redwood to attach SOC2 and ISO certs and subprocessor list with redlines.
